title: A Nonunimodal Acyclic Polynomial with All Roots in the Left Half-Plane
summary: Let $A(G,x)$ count vertex subsets of a graph $G$ that induce forests, by their cardinalities. Barton, Brown, and Pike asked whether failure of coefficient unimodality forces $A(G,x)$ to have a root with positive real part. We give a negative answer. The join of $K_{46}$ with three disjoint copies of $P_3$ has a nonunimodal acyclic polynomial of degree nine, yet all its complex roots have strictly negative real part.
